_doc: The watercraft on the water at the scene date — three schooners moored in the reach below the Dearborn drawbridge and TWO MORE AT THE WOLF POINT LANDINGS (T-0122), rowboats on the water and drawn up at the South Water and the Wolf Point banks, and two bark canoes at the fort landing. Every boat is unmanned: L1 stands, no crews and no figures. AUTHORED, not generated — no rule can derive where a boat lay, so each position is an invention stated in its own note and claimed at docs/LIBERTIES.md L146. Drawn at load by renderers/web/js/boats.js, which refuses a boat its own water cannot carry.
name: The boats on the river
coordinates: Local East-North-Up metres from data/datum.json's origin. The water surface is Z = 0 by construction (data/datum.json § vertical); heading_deg is measured from local east, counter-clockwise.

existence.note: THAT BOATS WERE ON THIS RIVER IS AS CLOSE TO CERTAIN AS ANYTHING THIS LAYER TOUCHES, AND EVERY INDIVIDUAL HULL IS INVENTED. What is held: the 2026-08-18 owner brief (data/sources/assets/owner_brief_2026_08_18/README.md) — images 2 and 3, the two Dearborn drawbridge engravings, show schooner-rigged vessels moored close by the bridge and masts crowding the reach below it, and image 11, the South Water 1834 view, shows rowboats on the water and at the bank; the 2026-08-11 fort views (data/sources/assets/prefire_views_kevin_2026_08/README.md) put bark canoes on the fort reach, and plate "11" of that same set (prefire_views_kevin_2026_08/p6_0.png) hangs SHIP MASTS behind the Green Tree Tavern's roofline at Wolf Point, as the Braunhold/Trowbridge views of the same quarter do — which is the whole warrant for the two schooners now moored at the Wolf Point landings (T-0122); and Andreas records the schooner Illinois, the first vessel through the new cut, cheered at Newberry & Dole's wharf on 12 July 1834 — schooners were lake carriers in this harbour a year before the scene date. What is NOT held, anywhere this project has reached: the name, position, heading or rig of any particular vessel in the river on 1835-07-01. So no hull here claims to be a recorded boat — the Illinois herself is deliberately NOT drawn or named, because putting a named vessel at a berth on a date is a claim no source makes — and every boat is graded reconstructed, placed under the owner's ruling of 2026-08-18, verbatim: 'you can add boats correct for the era! they would exist.' Claimed at docs/LIBERTIES.md L146.
existence.standing_constraint_note: The two bark canoes are watercraft of the fur trade, drawn unmanned from the committed fort plates that show them at this reach. They are equipment, not people: AGENTS.md's standing constraint on depicting Native presence stands in full — no figures, no encampment, no staging — and any depiction of the Potawatomi themselves remains out of scope pending consultation.

drawbridge_span_m.note: INVENTED AS A RULE, NOT A MEASUREMENT: no afloat boat may lie within 30 m of the Dearborn drawbridge's crossing line (local E 699.17), so the navigation span and its approaches stay clear for T-0071's bridge work. The figure is the bridge's own ~60 ft draw plus manoeuvring room, applied symmetrically. The layer refuses a boat inside it rather than nudging one out.

length_m.note: INVENTED. A small two-masted lake schooner of the 1830s grain: the early carriers into this river were vessels of roughly 50-100 tons, and 16.5 m overall is the restrained end of that class — chosen small because the river channel this project models gives under 3 m of water, and a larger hull would be a claim about the harbour's capacity as well as about a boat.

beam_m.note: INVENTED. About 3.4 beams to the length, the proportion of the working schooners in the drawbridge engravings; nothing measures any hull in this river.

draft_m.note: INVENTED, AND IT IS ALSO THE LAYER'S REFUSAL FLOOR: a schooner is drawn only where the committed heightfield gives at least draft plus 0.3 m of water under the whole hull, so every moored schooner demonstrably floats in its own berth. 1.5 m is a light-laden draft for the class — the loaded figure would refuse the whole river, which is the honest reading of why cargoes lightered.

mast_height_m.note: INVENTED. Mainmast above deck, foremast slightly shorter, both raked aft — the silhouette the engravings hang over the reach. Rigged bare: yards, booms and bowsprit, no sails bent on, because a moored and unmanned vessel with set canvas would be a small story nobody attests.

freeboard_m.note: INVENTED. Deck edge above the waterline amidships, light trim.

length_m.note: INVENTED. A workaday skiff of the size the South Water 1834 view draws at the bank — a one-or-two-man rowing boat, open, transom-sterned.

beam_m.note: INVENTED. Ordinary skiff proportion; nothing measures one here.

draft_m.note: INVENTED, and the refusal floor for an afloat skiff as the schooner's draft is for a schooner.

freeboard_m.note: INVENTED. Gunwale above the waterline afloat; a beached hull sits on the ground the heightfield gives instead.

length_m.note: INVENTED. Between the small hunting canoe and the freight canoe of the lakes trade; the committed fort plates draw canoes of about this presence at this reach and measure nothing.

beam_m.note: INVENTED. Slender, both ends alike and swept up — the form the plates draw.

draft_m.note: INVENTED. A bark hull barely wets its bilge; both canoes here are drawn up on the bank, so the figure is carried for completeness and the ground carries the hulls.

freeboard_m.note: INVENTED. Gunwale height, ends rising above it.

geometry_note: The record owns every CLAIM about the water — which boats, of what type and size, where each lies and at what heading, and the clearances they keep. How a hull becomes triangles is the renderer's: the station count of the loft, the chine line, the thwarts, the mast rake are in renderers/web/js/boats.js, the same division data/wharves/ makes with wharves.js. An AFLOAT boat's vertical position is the water plane's (Z = 0 less its own draft) and a BEACHED boat's is the terrain's at its own keel line, sampled at load — the bridge's lesson (T-0001) again: no height here is authored beside the mesh.
not_drawn: NO CREW, NO FIGURES, NO CARGO ON DECK, NO SET SAILS, NO VESSEL NAMES. L1 ships no human figures, uniformly; a named hull would claim a berth on a date no source gives; and set canvas on an unmanned moored vessel is a story, not a reconstruction. The schooner Illinois is deliberately not among these boats — see the existence note. Nothing lies at the wharves themselves: the wharf record's own not-drawn clause (no vessel at the docks) still holds, and these boats ride the open reaches instead.

boats.name: A lake schooner, moored
boats.symbolic_location: In the reach of the main stem below the Dearborn Street drawbridge
boats.note: INVENTED POSITION. The westernmost of the three schooners in the reach below the Dearborn drawbridge — the stretch image 3 of the 2026-08-18 brief shows crowded with masts. Her hull's west end lies about 52 m east of the drawbridge crossing line, well clear of the 30 m navigation clearance. The committed heightfield gives 2.9-3.0 m of water along her keel.

boats.name: A lake schooner, moored
boats.symbolic_location: In the reach of the main stem below the Dearborn Street drawbridge
boats.note: INVENTED POSITION. Mid-reach, about 45 m below her neighbour, heading a few degrees off hers — moored vessels in a river lie roughly with the channel and exactly alike only in a diagram. 2.7-2.8 m of water along the keel.

boats.name: A lake schooner, moored
boats.symbolic_location: In the reach of the main stem below the Dearborn Street drawbridge, toward the bend at the fort reach
boats.note: INVENTED POSITION. The easternmost of the three, toward the bend at the fort reach. 2.9-3.1 m of water along the keel.

boats.name: A lake schooner, moored
boats.symbolic_location: In the branch reach above the forks, moored off the west bank at Wolf Point
boats.note: INVENTED POSITION, AND THE BERTH IS DERIVED RATHER THAN CHOSEN. She lies head up the branch, 14.5 m off the west bank as the committed heightfield draws it, abreast the Wolf Point frontages the town already stands there — the Walker Meeting House and the Robinson and Caldwell cabins. The offset is not a taste: it is close to the westernmost line on this reach where the heightfield gives a light-laden 1.5 m schooner her draft plus the layer's 0.3 m under the keel along the whole hull, which comes out at 2.07-2.11 m of water. Any nearer the bank and the layer refuses her. WHAT SHE IS FOR: plate 11 of the 2026-08-11 prefire views and the Braunhold view both hang ship masts over the Wolf Point roofs, and until now the forks held nothing while the only masts in the scene stood 900 m east.

boats.name: A lake schooner, moored
boats.symbolic_location: In the South Branch reach below the forks, off the west bank abreast Robert Kinzie's store
boats.note: INVENTED POSITION, DERIVED THE SAME WAY. She lies with the reach below the forks, 36 m off the west bank abreast Robert A. Kinzie's store — the landing T-0107 is open on — at close to the westernmost line the heightfield floats her: 1.81 m of water at her shallowest keel sample against the 1.80 m the layer demands. This reach is the one open water on the Green Tree Tavern's own eastward sight line, which is why a second hull stands here rather than beside the first.

boats.name: A rowboat on the water
boats.symbolic_location: Off the South Water Street bank, west of the merchant landings
boats.note: INVENTED POSITION. Lying off the South Water bank between the merchant landings — image 11 of the 2026-08-18 brief, the South Water 1834 view, draws rowboats on this water. About 2.3 m under her; kept off the wharf decks themselves, whose record draws no vessel.

boats.name: A rowboat on the water
boats.symbolic_location: Off the South Water Street bank, west of the merchant landings
boats.note: INVENTED POSITION. Her neighbour, a boat-length and a half east and swung to a different heading. About 2.4 m under her; some 24 m west of Jones's landing.

boats.name: A rowboat drawn up at the bank
boats.symbolic_location: At the water's edge of the South Water Street bank
boats.note: INVENTED POSITION. Drawn up at the water's edge of the South Water bank, bow to the grass — the committed ground here lies at the waterline, so her stern wets and her bow rides the bank, which is what image 11 draws. The hull sits on the terrain's own surface, sampled at load.

boats.name: A rowboat drawn up at the bank
boats.symbolic_location: At the water's edge of the South Water Street bank
boats.note: INVENTED POSITION. Beside her neighbour, a little higher up the bank on ground just proud of the water — two skiffs hauled out side by side read as a working bank, one alone reads as an accident.

boats.name: A rowboat on the water
boats.symbolic_location: Off the west bank at Wolf Point, inside the schooners' berths
boats.note: INVENTED POSITION. A skiff lying 8 m off the west bank inside the schooner's berth, where the heightfield gives 1.2 m of water — deep for a 0.2 m draft and shoal for anything else, which is the whole reason a landing on this bank worked by boat. Nothing attests this skiff; the type is the one image 11 of the 2026-08-18 brief draws on the water at South Water Street.

boats.name: A rowboat drawn up at the bank
boats.symbolic_location: At the water's edge of the west bank at Wolf Point, below the log cabins
boats.note: INVENTED POSITION. Hauled out on the west bank below the Wolf Point cabins, on committed ground 0.42 m above the water surface with the waterline four metres off her stern. The hull rides the terrain's own surface, sampled at load; no height is authored beside it.

boats.name: A bark canoe at the fort landing
boats.symbolic_location: On the bank below Fort Dearborn, at the fort reach
boats.note: INVENTED POSITION. Drawn up on the bank below Fort Dearborn's rising ground, where the committed 2026-08-11 fort plates put bark canoes at the water. Unmanned, like everything on this layer — see the record's standing-constraint note. The bank track from the fort's north gate (T-0099) would come down to about this reach.

boats.name: A bark canoe at the fort landing
boats.symbolic_location: On the bank below Fort Dearborn, at the fort reach
boats.note: INVENTED POSITION. Beside the first, a shoulder higher on the bank and at its own angle — the plates draw canoes in company, not a lone exhibit.
